transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Liam, Maya, Noah (Redwood) — Derek, Priya, Samir, Ava, Ethan (Hyperlane)

[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, walk through the connector design, packaging for marketplace and onprem helm chart, then open Q&A.
[00:18] Derek Wong: yep, thanks. we really wanna make sure the onprem flow is smooth for our enterprise customers — kms, vpc and the audit trails are must haves.
[00:30] Maya Ortiz: ok, i'll share my screen — this is a rough diagram of the connector patterns we propose: hosted proxy, dedicated cluster, and full onprem helm chart. the helm chart is the one we need to marry to Hyperlane's agent and service mesh.
[00:52] Priya Mehta: when you say "agent", you mean a small sidecar that does routing to the redwood runtime? is that pluggable?
[01:05] Maya Ortiz: yes sidecar or daemonset, pluggable. we typically provide a lightweight adapter that handles auth, local caching of KV cache — sorry, kv cash in the transcription earlier — yeah kv cache. it uses prefix caching to reduce token cost.
[01:30] Ethan Park: for our infra we prefer daemonset; fewer moving parts. also need to confirm CNI compatibility — calico and aws-vpc. any pain points there?
[01:48] Noah Rivera: we've deployed with calico and aws-vpc before. the biggest friction tends to be IAM policies for nodes that need to reach the redwood control plane for telemetry and model pull.
[02:05] Samir Patel: security questions — does the connector allow customer-managed KMS? we need HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest and we want zero-key transmission to redwood.
[02:20] Maya Ortiz: yes, support for customer-managed keys is in scope. the control plane talks over TLS and we can do envelope encryption so keys never leave your KMS. we'll need the KMS API endpoints and a service principal or role.
[02:40] Priya Mehta: ok do you have templates for IAM role assumption and STS? our security team will want to see example policies.
[02:50] Liam Chen: we'll attach sample IAM and an architectural runbook after the call.
[03:00] -- auto-summary insertion (may be rough) --
[03:15] Ava Long: from a product perspective, how will marketplace listing look? we want a single-click install for customers that pulls a vetted chart and sets the correct defaults.
[03:30] Maya Ortiz: marketplace listing will point to an official Helm chart repo and an operator. we'll provide quickstart options: 1-click deploy via marketplace portal that spins up an instance on the customer's cloud or a pointer to the onprem bundle for air-gapped installs.
[03:52] Derek Wong: for air-gapped installs we need an offline bundle and clear checksum verification and an installation script.
[04:05] Maya Ortiz: yes offline tarball plus signed attestations. we'll coordinate checksums and a release signing process.
[04:20] Priya Mehta: another thing — quantization. we run some models on inference accelerators and want to understand how you plan to deliver quantized model variants versus full fp16. do you plan to ship quantized binaries in the chart?
[04:38] Maya Ortiz: good question. plan is to allow customers to select model variant during install: float16, int8 quantized, or our adaptive quant profiles. the chart references model artifacts stored in a registry. for onprem we support pulling from a customer S3 or from Redwood model artifacts if they opt in.
[05:00] Ethan Park: will the model artifacts be OCI images or artifacts in an S3-style bucket? we prefer OCI images for better integrity and scanning.
[05:12] Noah Rivera: we can support OCI image distribution for models; that aligns well with Helm and image pull.
[05:24] Samir Patel: telemetry — we need to be sure pii is not leaked. what telemetry is sent back to redwood?
[05:36] Maya Ortiz: we only collect operational metrics at rollout by default: token counts, latency histograms, errors. payloads are not shipped. we have a privacy knob and can anonymize traces. still, we will need to capture sample prompts for quality evals only with explicit consent.
[05:56] Priya Mehta: can we opt into local-only telemetry and ship aggregated metrics to your console?
[06:06] Maya Ortiz: yes, there's a local aggregation mode and a push-only aggregated metrics endpoint.
[06:15] Derek Wong: SLA expectations — what's the plan for canary and fallback? our customers want predictable behavior if your hosted variant has an outage.
[06:29] Liam Chen: we recommend a routing policy in the chart: primary runtime with fallback pinned to a smaller local quantized model. canary rollouts are baked in via helm hooks and we can do progressive traffic shift.
[06:45] Priya Mehta: and how is billing metered for onprem? metering has to tie to our billing or to your usage billing depending on contract.
[06:56] Noah Rivera: metering can be plugin-based: we ship an agent that aggregates token counts and emits a signed usage blob to your billing endpoint or to Redwood for invoicing. Hyperlane can choose which to use.
[07:16] Ava Long: ok good. next, packaging: do you have a recommended directory structure for the chart and operator?
[07:26] Maya Ortiz: yes standard helm layout. we'll provide a values.yaml with three profiles: dev, prod, airgap. each profile toggles model pull strategy, telemetry, and caching sizes.
[07:44] -- timestamp skips and some crosstalk --
[08:10] Priya Mehta: about model pull — for customers in regulated sectors, pulling from Redwood public registry isn't allowed. we need to ensure the chart can reference private registries and also support offline import.
[08:25] Maya Ortiz: we'll document the private registry steps and provide an offline import script that preloads model OCI images into your registry.
[08:35] Derek Wong: can we add a pre-install hook that validates IAM and network egress rules? that would reduce friction.
[08:46] Maya Ortiz: yep we can include pre-install checks and an egress test.
[09:00] Ethan Park: performance benchmarks — what's realistic for an n1-standard with a single A10/30 or equivalent GPU?
[09:10] Noah Rivera: depends on model size and sequence length. for a 13B model at 512 tokens, you'd expect X tokens/sec in fp16; quantized int8 will be faster per GPU but may change latency distribution. we'll run a lab with your workload.
[09:35] Ethan Park: i'll send the QPS and p95 targets after the call.
[09:42] -- filler and partial words, some mis-transcriptions --
[12:00] Samir Patel: one more security thing — audit logs for admin actions and token issuance. we need those forwarded to our SIEM.
[12:12] Maya Ortiz: we can forward audit logs via syslog or a managed collector; we also support structured JSON over HTTPS to your telemetry endpoint.
[12:25] Derek Wong: awesome.
[12:30] Ava Long: i had a question about license and distribution — if we list on marketplace, do customers see Hudson... sorry i mean Redwood branding?
[12:40] Liam Chen: marketplace listing can be co-branded. listing page will show Hyperlane as the publisher and Redwood as runtime provider; we can agree the language.
[12:56] Priya Mehta: for canary routing, who owns the traffic policy? us or Redwood?
[13:04] Maya Ortiz: ownership is configurable; typically Hyperlane owns the k8s routing and Redwood provides a routing library and helm defaults.
[13:20] Derek Wong: about the pilot — what's in scope for the 2-week lab?
[13:27] Liam Chen: 2-week lab: deploy helm chart in your lab, validate KMS and OCI model pulls, run representative workloads for perf and token accounting, and test canary/fallback behavior.
[13:40] Priya Mehta: do you need remote access to our cluster for the pilot?
[13:46] Maya Ortiz: preferred is a test cluster we can SSH into or an ephemeral cluster we set up with your sample dataset. remote access is optional; we can do a white-glove setup or hand-off docs.
[14:05] Ethan Park: we'd prefer a hand-off + runbook, but can agree to brief remote debugging sessions.
[14:14] -- mid-call summary notes inserted by auto-transcribe --
[15:00] Maya Ortiz: recapping: artifacts to share — helm skeleton, IAM role samples, offline bundle steps, and security questionnaire. action items we'll track in the ticket.
[15:18] Liam Chen: also i'll put together a pilot statement of work and pricing for reserved capacity vs bring-your-own-runtime options.
[15:30] Derek Wong: can you also include a timing estimate for certifying our operator into the marketplace? we want dates.
[15:42] Liam Chen: certification typically takes 3 weeks once artifacts are in, plus UAT. we'll propose a schedule in the SOW.
[16:00] Priya Mehta: question about model updates — how do we handle rolling model updates without downtime?
[16:12] Noah Rivera: we support hot swap via KV cache priming and staged rollout. the runtime will keep the old model serving until the new model warms the cache. helm hooks coordinate the rollout.
[16:30] Samir Patel: thanks.
[16:36] Ava Long: any blockers on compliance?
[16:40] Liam Chen: none we've seen; you'll need to provide SOC artifacts — we'll hand over our SOC2 report and the compliance checklist.
[16:50] Priya Mehta: ok. can you confirm support for FIPS endpoints? some gov customers require that.
[16:58] Maya Ortiz: yes FIPS endpoints via our private deployment offering. we'll include notes for FIPS and GovCloud in the runbook.
[17:10] Ethan Park: sound good. i'll gather the workload and KMS info.
[17:15] Derek Wong: and i'll coordinate the pilot resources.
[17:22] -- closing minutes: recap and next steps --
[17:40] Liam Chen: great, recap of next steps: maya will push initial helm repo by 2027-08-11; priya and team to send KMS details and workload by 2027-08-07; samir to return security questionnaire by 2027-08-09; liam to send SOW and pilot pricing by 2027-08-10.
[17:58] Priya Mehta: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[18:05] Liam Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in thread and schedule kickoff for the pilot.

End of transcript.
